name: Can I replace my bathroom countertop without replacing the entire vanity cabinet?

mainEntity.name: Can I replace my bathroom countertop without replacing the entire vanity cabinet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can install a new countertop on an existing vanity provided the cabinet boxes are structurally solid, level, and free of moisture damage. Before ordering stone, we inspect your vanity framing and sub-bases. Heavy slabs such as marble or thick quartz require solid structural support; sagging face frames, swollen particleboard, or dry rot must be repaired first. If your layout works well and the cabinet wood is stable, keeping the vanity and swapping just the countertop, sink, and faucet is a cost-effective way to modernize a bathroom.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, as long as the existing vanity frame is level, structurally sound, and free of water damage. Heavy stone slabs require solid support that can be reinforced if needed.
